headword: {公衆電話|こうしゅうでんわ}

definitions.explanation: A telephone available for public use, typically operated with coins or prepaid cards. Still found in Japan at stations and convenience stores.

examples.japanese: {公衆電話|こうしゅうでんわ}はどこですか。
{駅|えき}の{前|まえ}に{公衆電話|こうしゅうでんわ}がある。
examples.english: There is a payphone in front of the station.

examples.japanese: {携帯|けいたい}の{電池|でんち}が{切|き}れたので、{公衆電話|こうしゅうでんわ}から{電話|でんわ}をかけた。
examples.english: My phone battery died, so I made a call from a payphone.

notes:
USAGE:
{公衆電話|こうしゅうでんわ} combines {公衆|こうしゅう} (public) and {電話|でんわ} (telephone). Although their numbers have decreased with the spread of mobile phones, payphones remain in Japan for emergency use. Green payphones accept テレホンカード (telephone cards) and coins.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {公衆電話|こうしゅうでんわ}をかける (to make a call from a payphone)
- {公衆電話|こうしゅうでんわ}ボックス (phone booth)
- {公衆電話|こうしゅうでんわ}の{設置場所|せっちばしょ} (payphone location)
